Bill.BriefDescription: Changing provisions concerning limitation of claims under a construction contract.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to claims under a construction contract; amendingRCW 4.24.370 and 4.24.380; and adding a new section to chapter 4.24RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 4.24 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Any clause in a construction contract that purports to waive,release, or extinguish the claim rights of a contractor, subcontractor,or supplier to damages or an equitable adjustment based on failure tosubmit claim notice or claimrelated documentation in a specified timeframe or form is waived to the extent that the contractor,subcontractor, or supplier shows by a preponderance of the evidencethat: (a) The party to whom the claim is being made had knowledge of andconsented to the actions of the contractor, subcontractor, or supplierthat are the basis of the claim; and (b) The actions of the contractor, subcontractor, or supplier thatare the basis of the claim benefited the party to whom the claim isbeing made. p. 1 HB 1765 (2) For purposes of this section, "construction contract" has thesame meaning as the term is defined in RCW 4.24.370.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 4.24.370 and 1979 ex.s. c 264 s 2 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: "Construction contract" for purposes of RCW 4.24.360 and section 1of this act means any contract or agreement for the construction,alteration, repair, addition to, subtraction from, improvement to, ormaintenance of, any building, highway, road, railroad, excavation, orother structure, project, development, or improvement attached to realestate, including moving and demolition in connection therewith.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 4.24.380 and 1979 ex.s. c 264 s 3 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The provisions of RCW 4.24.360 shall apply to contracts oragreements entered into after September 1, 1979. (2) Section 1 of this act applies to contracts or agreementsentered into on or after the effective date of this act.
